footer.tagline: Casting management platform for casting directors and talent agencies.

items.a: Castiqq is a casting management platform. Casting directors define projects and roles, collect audition videos from talent, and decide together with their team by reviewing and rating on one screen. Talent agencies manage their roster, contracts, jobs and receivables. Both sides work on the same platform, connected to each other.
Two user types: casting directors working at production companies or freelance, and talent agencies representing actors. You pick your side at signup and the interface adapts accordingly.

items.q: Do actors need to create an account?
items.a: No. The casting director shares a passwordless application link; talent can submit an audition video and profile details through it without signing up.

items.q: How do casting directors and talent agencies connect?
items.a: A casting director shares a role, including criteria and budget, with a talent agency. The agency sees it under Incoming Roles and pitches suitable talent from its roster with fees attached. The casting director reviews every pitch on one screen, marks favourites and can export to PDF. Neither organization accesses the other's data directly; every shared record travels as a snapshot.

items.q: What financial calculations does the agency side handle?
items.a: For each job, withholding tax is deducted from the gross amount to derive the net figure and the agency commission automatically. A 20% withholding rate is applied by default for talent invoicing as self-employed, and can be adjusted. Partial payments, overdue receivables and uncollected commissions are tracked separately.

items.q: How does it prevent pitching an actor to competing brands?
items.a: Commercial jobs record a brand category. When pitching an actor, the system warns you if an unexpired exclusivity exists in the same category. Sixteen brand categories are predefined and the warning clears itself once the exclusivity expires.
One plan per side: the Casting Director plan is 1,999 TRY per month and the Talent Agency plan is 4,999 TRY per month. There is no per-seat pricing. Both plans include a 14-day free trial.

Each organization's data is separated at the database level using row-level security policies, so one organization cannot see another's records. The platform is designed to comply with KVKK and GDPR, and the sub-processors used are listed explicitly in the privacy policy.

items.q: Which languages does the interface support?
items.a: Turkish and English. The language preference is stored per user, so teams working with international productions can operate in different languages within the same account.

problem.label: Sound Familiar
problem.title: The hard part of casting isn't finding talent — it's holding the process together
problem.intro: Casting usually ends up scattered across three tools: videos in WhatsApp or Drive, the candidate list in Excel, decisions buried in an email thread. That gap is where Castiqq came from.

items.title: Videos everywhere
items.desc: Forty tapes from forty actors — some on WhatsApp, some behind a Drive link, some on an expired WeTransfer. Remembering which tape belongs to which role is on you.

items.title: Decisions evaporate
items.desc: The director likes one actor, the producer another. Two weeks later nobody remembers who said what, and you rewatch the same tape from scratch.

items.title: The list goes stale
items.desc: Three versions of the same spreadsheet circulate. Who was cut and who was called back depends on which file you opened.

items.title: Agency traffic is tiring
items.desc: Every agency pitches in a different format: a PDF here, a WhatsApp message there, sometimes just a list of names. You assemble them by hand to compare.

workflow.label: How It Works
workflow.title: From role definition to final selection

steps.title: Define the project and its roles
steps.desc: Roles live under each project. You set the age range, gender, height, required skills and city. You can attach a script excerpt and track the role's status — open, casting, filled.

steps.title: Invite talent
steps.desc: You share a passwordless application link. Talent submits an audition video and profile details without creating an account. You can also invite directly from your existing talent pool.

steps.title: Review with your team
steps.desc: Every video collects into one list per role. While watching you rate out of five stars, tag, and pin a note to the exact moment. Everyone sees the same screen and every comment is attributed.

steps.title: Share the shortlist and decide
steps.desc: Reorder candidates by drag and drop, update their status — shortlisted, callback, selected — and send your shortlist to the producer with a shareable link.

matching.label: The Time Saver
matching.title: Matching talent surfaces from your pool automatically
matching.desc: Instead of searching a pool of hundreds by hand, entering the role's criteria surfaces the people who fit. Gender and age act as hard filters; skills, city and availability feed a score. Each match shows badges explaining why it fits, and you add candidates in one click.
points: Age, height, gender, skills and city criteria
One-click add to the candidate list

bridge.label: The Agency Link
bridge.title: Agency pitches arrive in one format
bridge.desc: You can share a role directly with a talent agency — criteria, budget and script excerpt included. The agency pitches suitable talent from its roster with fees attached. Every pitch lands on the same screen in the same format: photos, physical attributes, experience, self-tape links and the asking fee side by side. Mark your favourites, print as a presentation or export to PDF.
bridge.note: Neither organization accesses the other's data. Every shared record travels as a snapshot — the agency can't see your projects, and you can't see the agency's roster financials.

items.q: Can the rest of my team see the videos?
items.a: Yes. You invite teammates by email; everyone sees the same candidate list and videos and adds their own rating and notes. Every comment is attributed by name and date.

items.q: How do I work with talent agencies?
